stories.title: Sr. Housing Developer Advancing 242-Unit Plano Independent Living Facility
stories.excerpt: While not a sure thing, Integrated Senior Lifestyles is getting closer to building a 242-unit senior housing project in Plano. The planning commission has okayed the venture, with only the city council to provide its okay for it to become final. The development is planned for construction near Ohio Drive and Park Boulevard at the former site of the Plano Athletic Club, which closed in 2025. The new independent living facility from Integrated Senior Lifestyles will be a 5-story building with an abundance of amenities. They include restaurant-style dining, a coffee bistro, and a bar lounge, an indoor/outdoor pool, a recovery sauna, a hot tub, a fitness center, a yoga studio, and an indoor pickleball court. Other amenities include a library, an art studio, a game room, a media room, an on-site salon, concierge support, and scheduled transportation. The post Sr. Housing Developer Advancing 242-Unit Plano Independent Living Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Integrated Senior Lifestyles, 242-unit independent living, Plano planning commission approved
Former Plano Athletic Club site, Ohio Drive/Park Boulevard, 5-story facility
City council final approval needed; high-amenity model with dining, pool, fitness
stories.summary: Integrated Senior Lifestyles has cleared the planning commission for a 242-unit independent living facility in Plano, Texas on the former Plano Athletic Club site. The five-story building will feature premium amenities including restaurant dining, pools, fitness center, and indoor pickleball court. Final city council approval is pending.
stories.impact: Senior housing supply in high-growth Dallas suburbs signals strong demographic tailwinds (aging boomers, affluent retirees) and represents an alternative yield-generating product class. Approval progression in Plano suggests zoning receptivity to senior residential; watch Dallas-Fort Worth suburban markets for similar conversions of obsolete retail/recreation properties into age-restricted multifamily—a lower-competition development play as traditional apartment developers focus on workforce housing.

stories.title: Ownership Group Acquires Providence Place Mall Out of Receivership
stories.excerpt: The Providence Place shopping center, in receivership since November 2024, has new ownership. A group consisting of Pyramid Management Group, Paolino Properties and DW Partners has closed on the acquisition of Rhode Island’s largest mall for a reported $133 million. The transaction represents the beginning of a comprehensive repositioning and revitalization process for the 27-year-old center, Pyramid said in a statement. “Pyramid is hitting the ground running, and our team is already hard at work bringing new brands, state-of-the-art security technology, and center-wide improvements to the shopping center,” said Stephen J. Congel, CEO of Syracuse, NY-based Pyramid. Added Joseph R. Paolino, Jr., managing partner of Paolino Properties. “There is something especially meaningful about Pyramid returning to a property they originally developed and managed, and we have tremendous confidence in the experience and expertise they bring to its operation.” For Paolino, the acquisition represents a return as well: he was mayor of Providence when the idea of a large-scale shopping center was first broached, and he later helped advance the project as the state’s economic development director. The post Ownership Group Acquires Providence Place Mall Out of Receivership appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pyramid Management Group, Paolino Properties, DW Partners acquire Providence Place for $133 million
Rhode Island's largest mall, in receivership since November 2024, now repositioned
Pyramid returning to original developer/manager role; multi-tenant repositioning announced
stories.summary: A consortium led by Pyramid Management Group acquired Rhode Island's largest shopping mall, Providence Place, out of receivership for $133 million. The 27-year-old center has been undergoing repositioning efforts, with new branding, security upgrades, and tenant recruitment underway. Pyramid originally developed and managed the property.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; retail mall repositioning does not typically drive apartment demand. However, successful urban mall revitalization can stabilize nearby commercial corridors and support infill residential development if ground-floor retail activation improves the market's perception. Monitor whether Providence Place reposition generates mixed-use residential development momentum downtown.

stories.title: Leasing Underway at Massive Forney Mixed-Use Development
stories.excerpt: StreetLevel Investments, a Texas-based developer, announced that its first tenants have opened at Village at Gateway, a multi-phase 152-acre mixed-use development in booming Forney, Texas. Located at North Gateway Boulevard and U.S. Highway 80 in the 2,000-acre Gateway master planned development, Phase 1 will feature 750,000 square feet of premium retail, entertainment and restaurants. groundbreaking was November 2024. Village at Gateway is the largest ground-up retail development in the Southwest United States. Designed by GFF with Ridgemont Commercial Construction serving as the general contractor, Village at Gateway is anchored by Target, Home Depot and H-E-B. Upon full completion, it will feature an additional 120,000 square feet of retail, service, and restaurant concepts. It will also include nine outparcels, future multi-family residential. David Copeland and Ryan Griffin of Edge Realty Partners are handling retail leasing and sales at the property. The post Leasing Underway at Massive Forney Mixed-Use Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: StreetLevel Investments, Village at Gateway, 152-acre mixed-use Forney, Texas groundbreaking November 2024
Phase 1: 750,000 sq ft retail; Target, Home Depot, H-E-B anchors; leasing underway
Nine outparcels reserved for future multi-family residential on 2,000-acre master plan
stories.summary: StreetLevel Investments announced first tenant openings at Village at Gateway, a 152-acre mixed-use development in Forney, Texas. Phase 1 features 750,000 square feet of retail anchored by Target, Home Depot, and H-E-B, with leasing active. The master plan includes nine outparcels designated for future multi-family residential within the larger 2,000-acre Gateway development.
stories.impact: Forney's suburban growth corridor (northeast of Dallas) is benefiting from large-scale master-planned development anchored by major retailers, signaling population migration and household formation. The explicit carve-out of nine multi-family outparcels indicates strong demand signals; developers should monitor absorption of retail phase and timing of residential parcels—this is a greenfield market-capture opportunity before density prices in. Watch Forney job growth and household migration data for upstream multifamily underwriting.

stories.title: Anthropologie Selects Bluhawk Retail Plaza for Third Kansas City-Area Store
stories.excerpt: Bluhawk announced that Anthropologie will join the 277-acre mixed-use destination in summer 2027, marking the retailer’s third Kansas City-area location to date. Anthropologie is a modern, design-led lifestyle brand, and the store will occupy a prominent location at the heart of Bluhawk. “Anthropologie is a natural fit for Bluhawk as we continue building out the retail offering,” said Kent Price, president of Price Brothers, the developer and manager of Bluhawk. “Its breadth across fashion, home and lifestyle adds another dimension to the experience and complements the national brands taking shape across the project.” Anthropologie expands Bluhawk’s fashion and lifestyle offering as the destination continues to grow. The brand joins other recently announced tenants at Bluhawk, including L.L.Bean, Barnes & Noble, J.Crew Factory and the newly opened Buckle. Bluhawk is a master-planned development in Overland Park, Kansas, that features a multi-sport and entertainment complex with retail, dining, residential, office, hospitality, healthcare, green space and amenities. The post Anthropologie Selects Bluhawk Retail Plaza for Third Kansas City-Area Store appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Anthropologie third Kansas City-area store, Bluhawk mixed-use, summer 2027 opening
277-acre Bluhawk destination (Overland Park, Kansas) adds L.L.Bean, Barnes & Noble, J.Crew Factory
Master plan includes retail, dining, residential, office, healthcare, hospitality
stories.summary: Anthropologie will open its third Kansas City-area location at Bluhawk, a 277-acre mixed-use development in Overland Park, Kansas, in summer 2027. The retail expansion complements recently announced or opened tenants including L.L.Bean, Barnes & Noble, J.Crew Factory, and The Buckle. Bluhawk is a master-planned community featuring retail, dining, residential, office, hospitality, and healthcare.
stories.impact: Overland Park/Kansas City suburban retail agglomeration and high-end brand recruitment signals affluent demographic concentration and household growth. The explicit residential component of Bluhawk's master plan positions it as a suburban lifestyle destination; premium retailers (Anthropologie, L.L.Bean) attract white-collar workers and higher-income renters. Track Bluhawk residential timeline and unit count—this is a branded lifestyle/mixed-use market where luxury garden or mid-rise residential can command premium rents.

stories.title: Gilbane, Purdue Fort Wayne Host Ribbon Cutting for 600-Bed Student Housing Complex
stories.excerpt: Gilbane and Purdue University Fort Wayne (PFW) celebrated the ribbon-cutting of Trace, a student housing complex on PFW’s North Campus, made possible through a public-private partnership. Located at 5104 Meeks Drive near Ginsberg Hall, the four-story, 213,000-square-foot apartment complex offers 601 beds across 176 units, ranging from studios to four-bedroom accommodations. Nearly half of the beds are reserved for university-contracted students, while the remaining beds will be available to other students enrolled at other colleges and universities, who will lease directly with the complex.  “Trace is a testament to what can be achieved when a university and private developer align on a shared goal, and we’re proud to partner with Purdue to effectively and efficiently deliver new residences that further unlock its campus’ potential,” said Geoff Eisenacher, Executive Development Director, Gilbane Development. The project team includes Gilbane as the developer and construction manager, AVB as the design-builder, and Progressive AE as the architect. The complex will be owned by Strategic Facility Partners and operated by Inwood Management. The post Gilbane, Purdue Fort Wayne Host Ribbon Cutting for 600-Bed Student Housing Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gilbane and Purdue Fort Wayne, Trace student housing, 601 beds, 176 units, public-private partnership
Four-story, 213,000 sq ft, near Ginsberg Hall; nearly 50% university-contracted beds

stories.summary: Gilbane and Purdue University Fort Wayne celebrated the ribbon-cutting of Trace, a 601-bed student housing complex with 176 units on PFW's North Campus. The four-story, 213,000-square-foot complex is structured as a public-private partnership with nearly half of beds reserved for university-contracted students and the remainder available to other area college students. Strategic Facility Partners owns; Inwood Management operates.
stories.impact: University partnerships with institutional operators (Inwood, AvalonBay design) indicate stable cash-flow-focused student housing is being repositioned as lower-risk, longer-duration assets. Fort Wayne market is tertiary; this signals demand for student housing near mid-tier campuses with population pressures. For developers: student housing with mixed university/open-market lease structures offers hybrid revenue stability—watch for similar institutional structures in secondary markets where single-university exposure is being de-risked.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar acquired Zonda for $800 million cash; completed mid-2026

Zonda's proprietary lot-level development data and builder analytics serve over 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers. The acquisition gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home market.
stories.impact: This is primarily a single-family homebuilding market play, not direct multifamily. However, CoStar's integration of Zonda's lot-level data and builder software with its own CRE platforms signals convergence of residential real estate intelligence—watch whether CoStar bundles land/lot availability data into multifamily underwriting tools. For multifamily developers: improved lot-level supply data transparency may drive land-acquisition competition in master-planned communities and suburban infill markets, compressing basis assumptions.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: With a population of less than 6,000, little Bay Harbor Islands, Fla., is often overlooked – but not by Regency Development Group. Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? Michael Troyanovsky: A really valid question, because there were other hot spot areas that a lot of people were gravitating to when we first started buying Bay Harbor. We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. We opened up a big sales office here, and we plan to stay here for the future. Who are you finding is the target demographic for your units? It’s a little bit of a mix demographic-wise, but I would say a lot of people who, whether it’s local or international, really want boutique building living. I’ve had the pleasure of meeting with all the people who purchased in the building and so many customers over the last few years, and all of them have said pretty much the same thing. bullets: Regency Development Group, Bay Harbor Islands (pop. <6,000), four active residential projects since 2020
33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas operational

The firm views the area as an overlooked gem surrounded by affluent waterfront submarkets.
stories.impact: Micro-scale boutique residential development in high-cost South Florida waterfront markets signals land scarcity and builder focus on ultra-premium, low-density projects. Bay Harbor Islands' isolation and small population suggest limited volume play but attractive margins for luxury product. For Trammell Crow: this is a signal that Miami-area coastal infill is being absorbed by specialized niche builders; monitor whether larger developers can still compete on land basis or if future Biscayne Bay area growth flows to larger suburban markets (Forney-style) rather than constrained waterfront.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management acquires 25,504 sq ft retail condo, $17.3 million, 3900 Biscayne Boulevard
Quadro condo building, ground floor, tenants include Shade Store, Waterworks; Miami Design District adjacent
Design District expansion underway: $125M construction loan, Fouquet's Chipperfield project, mixed-use growth
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management purchased a 25,504-square-foot retail condo on the ground floor of the Quadro building at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard for $17.3 million. The asset fronts train tracks east of the Miami Design District and is leased to specialty retailers. The purchase occurs as the nearby Miami Design District undergoes major expansion, including a $125 million construction loan for a mixed-use Snøhetta-designed building.
stories.impact: Miami Design District's expansion and luxury brand concentration (LVMH partnership, David Chipperfield residential) create a halo effect for adjacent commercial real estate. However, Biscayne Boulevard corridor's train-track frontage and auto-oriented character limits pure upscale residential appeal. For multifamily developers: watch whether Design District's expansion drives demand for high-end downtown/midtown Miami apartments rather than waterfront or suburban Biscayne Boulevard—the mixed-use buildout may cannibalize retail and redirect residential demand inward.

stories.title: Now Is the Time to Buy in Commercial Real Estate: Morgan Stanley
stories.excerpt: Despite a bumpy economy and increasingly high Treasury yields, one global investment firm believes now is the time to pounce on U.S. commercial real estate. Commercial Observer spoke with Tony Charles, global head of research and strategy at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, who outlined the main takeaways from Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s mid-year 2026 real estate outlook. After a four-year recession, commercial real estate is now being repriced, giving investors a chance to acquire prime assets at low prices; supply is down across the board; and megatrends in AI, global supply chains, and aging demographics have opened up attractive entry points into infrastructure, retail and senior housing. “We certainly believe we’re entering the next up-cycle for real estate. It’s an attractive entry point,” Charles told CO in a Thursday interview. “And, given the repricing that’s now below replacement costs, we’re pretty confident in the next vintage of real estate investing.” Charles argued that the recent U.S. real estate downturn — which began in mid-2022 amid the Federal Reserve’s policy U-turn to hike interest rates coming out of COVID-19 — created “the longest downturn for real estate since the 1980s and early 1990s,” and that four years later, pricing is still down an average of 20 percent across the board. But he noted that “supply is down dramatically, so that’s obviously very helpful for real estate,” and that a strong structural macroeconomic backdrop — U.S. GDP grew 2.1 percent year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026 — has provided “a lot of green shoots that are beginning to show through.” He pointed out that CRE transaction activity increased 23 percent year-over-year in the U.S., institutional capital raising is up nearly 40 percent on the year, and that CRE debt originations are up around 20 percent year-over-year. bullets: Morgan Stanley: CRE entering up-cycle post-2022 downturn; repricing below replacement cost
Supply down across board; megatrends (AI, supply chains, aging) opening entry points
Senior housing, infrastructure, and retail identified as attractive sectors; confident next vintage performs
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing released its mid-year 2026 outlook, arguing that U.S. commercial real estate is now repriced below replacement cost after a four-year downturn beginning mid-2022. The firm notes supply is down across asset classes and identifies megatrends in AI, global supply chains, and aging demographics as creating attractive entry points. Senior housing, infrastructure, and retail are highlighted as attractive sectors with strong next-vintage performance potential.
stories.impact: This is a broad capital-market signal, not metro-specific, but it validates the macro timing for multifamily acquisition and development: repricing and supply tightness create a window for ground-up delivery to capture rent growth as demand recovers. The callout on aging demographics directly supports Regency (Article 7) and Integrated Senior Lifestyles (Article 1) strategies. Multifamily developers should lock in land and financing in primary and secondary markets NOW before replacement-cost repricing ends and cap rates normalize—window is tightening as sentiment shifts.

stories.title: Whole Foods to Open Daily Shop at Murray Hill’s 509 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has leased a 9,000-square-foot retail space in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. The 15-year deal occupies a ground-floor space and outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue, according to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Friday morning. The 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower, known as the Murray, was developed by Kahen Properties with Lalezarian Properties. A spokesperson for Whole Foods confirmed the lease in an email to Commercial Observer, but declined to share further details. Whole Foods’ newest Manhattan location will be on the smaller side. The store will follow the Amazon-owned grocer’s new Whole Foods Market Daily Shop format. The quick-trip urban shops sell grab-and-go meals alongside fresh produce, meat, bakery items and local specialty foods, according to the company’s website. The format was first rolled out in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024, and has since arrived in cities nationwide. Additional locations in Brooklyn and Hoboken, N.J., were announced late last year. Most recently, the grocer signed a lease for 8,121 square feet to open a daily shop at 1524 Second Avenue on the Upper East Side. Kahen Properties’ Majid Kahen signed the lease memorandum for the landlord, while Paul Hilliard, vice president of real estate at Whole Foods, signed for the grocer. It is unclear whether either party worked with an outside brokerage. The asking rent for the ground-floor space was not disclosed in the memorandum, but retail space in the nearby Herald Square area was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. Spokespeople for Kahen and Lalezarian Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Whole Foods Market leases 9,000 sq ft, Murray Hill (Manhattan), 509 Third Avenue, 15-year deal
Murray building (229-unit apartment tower) developed by Kahen Properties, Lalezarian; Whole Foods Daily Shop format
Daily Shop model first rolled out Lenox Hill 2024; expanding Brooklyn, Hoboken; urban convenience anchor
stories.summary: Whole Foods Market leased a 9,000-square-foot ground-floor retail space with outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood on a 15-year deal. The location will operate as a Whole Foods Daily Shop, a smaller convenience-oriented format featuring grab-and-go meals and fresh items. The concept debuted in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024 and is expanding to Brooklyn and Hoboken.
stories.impact: Whole Foods' Daily Shop format and ground-floor urban penetration signal grocery/fresh-food demand is shifting toward smaller, walkable infill locations within multifamily-dense neighborhoods. This validates mixed-use development with integrated grocery retail (e.g., Bluhawk, Village at Gateway). For multifamily developers in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Northeast urban markets: Whole Foods' 9,000 sq ft footprint (vs. traditional 40,000+ sq ft) and 15-year lease indicate anchor retailers now expect smaller, higher-rent urban formats—recalibrate ground-floor retail economics in new multifamily projects to reflect this smaller, premium-yield model.
